findings.action: Keep main deliverable concrete and most work on usable episodes
findings.recommendation: One meaningful rule parameter; reused runnable prototype; executed original and alternative four-query episodes with distinguishing demonstrations; bounded actual success/failure counts. Prefer native adapter/contract from start. Guard-only or scalar-only repair does not complete the main parametric duty.
findings.evidence: Old-contract return has no parametric patch and reports only 52/99 supported three-demo/four-query sampled lessons. This is useful safety repair but incomplete generation reliability.
findings.basis: static archive inspection plus reviewer-reported runtime outcomes

findings.recommendation: Choose changed surfaces and at most two relevant adversarial probes, retain Racket-backed labels and teaching evidence; no automatic whole battery/census or arbitrary output-count quota.
findings.evidence: Original inspected main duty named every boundary/export/verifier surface imperatively; parent has already replaced it with a relevant-surface menu. Recent returns report stalled 79000/80100 draw matrix and optional batteries exhausting useful check budget.
findings.basis: current source inspection plus reviewer feedback

findings.recommendation: Fix identifiability for supported original demonstrations and four actual queries. Check rotated assembly only if family/consumer supports it.
findings.evidence: review-8da147dd49409d94 reports ordinary 12/12 production lessons pass but optional two-demo rotations have 6/36 ambiguities.

findings.action: Avoid a new turn controller per generator
findings.recommendation: Keep four stored queries and public/private boundary; use existing projection helpers and document sequential consumer contract. Do not ask reviewers to implement inference policy or a turn controller in each task home.
findings.evidence: New duties require sequential reveal while repository ownership excludes inference policy. ARC-DESIGN correctly calls multi-query public container controller data.

findings.recommendation: One likely-hole probe and obvious local fix; no parametric peer work, no rerunning all unchanged task tests, and no fixed per-peer minimum test count. If major flaw found, retain minimal source-bound finding and stop.
findings.evidence: New split and explicit peer scope are good; older reviews report unchanged peers retested with 47 and 20 tests or 200 windows per difficulty.

findings.recommendation: Use native parametric manifest for source/evidence inventory. Keep runnable command and limits once in task notes/README, short summary plus paths in RESULTS/REVIEW. Do not handwrite duplicate hash ledgers or require owner qualification for a return.
findings.evidence: Native inventory helper is already implemented per current suggestion review-fdc6a9b2aee6af87:v0001:F1 and documented promotion route. Metadata validator deliberately validates disposition and source presence, not semantics.
findings.basis: current documentation and validator source; helper not rerun

findings.recommendation: PARAMETRIC-RULES read-scope paragraph should refer to bounded peers, legacy tickets only when explicitly assigned.
findings.evidence: Paragraph still says read the two selected tickets despite new no-ticket default.

findings.action: Prioritize existing friction instead of adding new requirements
findings.recommendation: When owner tooling time is available, fix hardcoded frozen test paths and process deadline/finalization handling; mark intentionally omitted task-linked proposal assets. Do not add another reviewer preflight, full packet extraction or checklist to compensate.
findings.evidence: Repeated current feedback on immutable nonportable tests, timeouts and missing proposal assets; not independently reproduced in this audit.

verdict: New 70/15/15 policy improves useful-work focus; keep explicit bounds and reduce checklist, rotation and packaging duplication. No evidence yet that new policy produces better training data.
